**C1 — part; DISPUTABLE: yes.** Teamwork “runs a collaborative multi-agent team”; projects are “a configuration of folders defining the environment and the scope of your agent.” Task-specific teams meet the explicit **part** rule. **Yes** is defensible if persistent, multi-agent project scopes count as areas of work; the documentation defines them primarily as execution environments. [Teamwork, introduction](https://antigravity.google/docs/teamwork/), [Projects, “What is a project?”](https://antigravity.google/docs/projects/).

**C2 — yes.** For the Teamwork unit identified under C1: “Captures your initial prompt, goals, constraints, and testable acceptance criteria.” The architecture separately defines “Core orchestration and execution roles,” including “Explorers” and “Workers.” The team has a recorded objective and reusable roles independent of individual instances. [Teamwork, roles and structured handoffs](https://antigravity.google/docs/teamwork/).

**C3 — part.** The plugin manifest’s `author` field records “Publisher attribution as a string”. This identifies a provider per asset, without establishing unique accountability per responsibility or capability. [Build plugins, field reference](https://antigravity.google/docs/build-plugins/).

**C4 — part; DISPUTABLE: yes.** A subagent’s description is a “Detailed description used by the planner to determine when to delegate tasks to this agent.” Capability descriptions and invocation identifiers support delegation, but the stated routing occurs in the planner. **Yes** is defensible if the supplied roster and invocation mechanism count as runtime capability lookup beyond that planner. [Custom subagents, frontmatter configuration](https://antigravity.google/docs/subagents/).
